finding.title: Fix ScheduleSpec.weekly/.rolling to throw ArgumentError instead of assert() (silently unenforced in release builds)

evidence.quote: Throws [ArgumentError] when [daysOfWeek] is empty or contains values

finding.why: WeeklySchedule and RollingSchedule enforce their invariants with Dart `assert()`, which the compiler strips out of release builds entirely (only active in debug/profile). Both factory doc comments explicitly promise 'Throws ArgumentError' — that promise is false in the exact build users run. `fromParts` (same file, line 63) feeds `daysOfWeek ?? const []` directly into `WeeklySchedule(...)` whenever the DB/JSON column is null, and the independent JSON codec path in stage_definition_repository_impl.dart:346-349 does the same for a missing `days_of_week`/`days` key, wrapped in a try/catch that only rescues the debug-mode AssertionError — in release it silently produces a `WeeklySchedule([])`. A stage with an empty day-list never matches any weekday, so its chazara review permanently stops being scheduled with no error, no log, and no user-facing signal.
finding.recommendation: Replace both asserts with explicit `if (...) throw ArgumentError(...)` (matching the pattern already used correctly by ScopeLevel/StageOrder/Pin/DayKind/CalendarSystem in the same directory) so the invariant holds in release builds too.
acceptance_criteria: ScheduleSpec.weekly([]) and ScheduleSpec.rolling(0)/.rolling(-1) throw ArgumentError when run under `flutter test` compiled in release/profile mode (or any assert-disabled run), not just debug.

New test/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec_test.dart exists and is wired into the test suite, covering empty/out-of-range daysOfWeek, non-positive windowSize, and fromParts with a null daysOfWeek column.
AG-5 mirroring restored: lib/core/domain/value_objects/schedule_spec.dart has a corresponding test file (currently missing).
